title: PRIM: Meta-Learned Bayesian Root Cause Analysis
claim: A model trained once offline on synthetic tasks from a prior performs instant zero-shot inference on new real systems.
layout: 2 rows (training/inference) feeding central model column, left-to-right, red highlights
description: A wide two-row diagram split by a dashed horizontal line. The top row, labeled TRAINING (offline, once), starts with a red 'RCA prior' box showing a small causal graph. An arrow leads to a stack of synthetic task cards with data tables, a symptom mask and the true root cause T. The bottom row, labeled INFERENCE (real system), starts with a black 'Real system' box showing servers and a factory. It leads to observed and intervened data tables plus a symptom mask. Both rows feed a central black PRIM block with Encoder, Alternating attention and Decoder, plus a red dashed box on averaging over graphs and mechanisms. On the right, bar charts show predicted scores with a red dashed loss arrow looping back, and root-cause scores with one bar highlighted in red. A stopwatch reads 7 ms. Red marks the key elements.
caption: Simplified overview of the PRIM PFN training and inference process. The RCA prior samples synthetic data (Dobs, Dint, m) with a known root cause T, and PRIM is trained until convergence. For a new real system, PRIM takes the observed data and symptom mask m and returns root-cause scores in a single forward pass, implicitly averaging over the unknown graph G and mechanisms f.
abstract: Root Cause Analysis (RCA) aims to identify the main drivers of anomalies in complex multivariate systems. The task is challenging due to the need for structural causal knowledge for some methods, and the computational cost of inference at test time. This paper introduces PRIM (Prior-fitted Root cause Identification with Meta-learning), a causal meta-learning approach that frames RCA as a Bayesian inference task over a prior of causal models. By marginalising out structural uncertainty, PRIM detects changes in the data-generating mechanism between normal and anomalous periods, infers distributional differences without explicit statistical testing, and implicitly learns causal structure without model fitting at test time. Following the simulation-based meta-learning paradigm of prior-fitted networks (PFNs), PRIM uses a transformer neural process (TNP) that jointly attends over normal and anomalous samples and the structural dependencies of nodes, enabling fast zero-shot inference in systems with up to 100 variables. Across synthetic benchmarks and two realistic benchmark datasets, PetShop and CausRCA, PRIM is competitive with other graph-free methods.
